'''Elisha Nelson Manning'''<ref>{{Cite web |last=O'Connor |first=Ian |date=December 27, 2019 |title=Two titles, 210 straight starts, one Eli: How Manning conquered New York |url=https://abc7ny.com/sports/two-titles-210-straight-starts-one-eli-how-manning-conquered-new-york/5787932/ |access-date=January 20, 2023 |website=ABC7 New York |language=en |archive-date=January 20, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230120214308/https://abc7ny.com/sports/two-titles-210-straight-starts-one-eli-how-manning-conquered-new-york/5787932/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=May 10, 2016 |title=Manning solution for Eli confusion: 'Call me Elisha' |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/manning-solution-for-eli-confusion-call-me-elisha-0ap3000000661094 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230120214304/https://www.nfl.com/news/manning-solution-for-eli-confusion-call-me-elisha-0ap3000000661094 |archive-date=January 20, 2023 |access-date=January 20, 2023 |website=[[NFL.com]] |language=en-US}}</ref> (born January 3, 1981) is an American former professional football [[quarterback]] who played in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for 16 seasons with the [[New York Giants]]. A member of the [[Manning family]], he is the youngest son of [[Archie Manning|Archie]], younger brother of [[Cooper Manning|Cooper]] and [[Peyton Manning|Peyton]], and uncle of [[Arch Manning|Arch]]. Manning played [[college football]] for the [[Ole Miss Rebels football|Ole Miss Rebels]], winning the [[Maxwell Award|Maxwell]] and [[Johnny Unitas Golden Arm Award|Johnny Unitas Golden Arm]] awards in 2003. He was selected [[List of first overall NFL draft picks|first overall]] in the [[2004 NFL draft]] by the [[San Diego Chargers]] and traded to the Giants during the draft.

Manning's greatest professional success was twice leading the Giants to underdog [[Super Bowl]] victories against the [[Brady–Belichick era|New England Patriots dynasty]] in [[Super Bowl XLII|Super Bowls XLII]] and [[Super Bowl XLVI|XLVI]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Silver |first=Nate |author-link=Nate Silver |date=January 12, 2015 |title=The Most Clutch Postseason Quarterback Of All Time Is Eli Manning |url=https://fivethirtyeight.com/features/the-most-clutch-postseason-quarterback-of-all-time-is-eli-manning/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171115083037/https://fivethirtyeight.com/features/the-most-clutch-postseason-quarterback-of-all-time-is-eli-manning/ |archive-date=November 15, 2017 |access-date=January 25, 2018 |website=FiveThirtyEight}}</ref> The former, which saw the [[Wild card (sports)|wild card]] Giants defeat a Patriots team that was the first to win all 16 regular season games, is regarded as one of the greatest sports upsets of all time.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mueller |first=Chris |date=May 18, 2022 |title='Do you believe in miracles? Yes!' Most memorable upsets in sports history |url=https://www.yardbarker.com/general_sports/articles/do_you_believe_in_miracles_yes_most_memorable_upsets_in_sports_history/s1__31370390 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220806115925/https://www.yardbarker.com/general_sports/articles/do_you_believe_in_miracles_yes_most_memorable_upsets_in_sports_history/s1__31370390 |archive-date=August 6, 2022 |access-date=August 17, 2022 |website=Yardbarker |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Chase |first=Jeff |date=January 26, 2012 |title=The 50 Biggest Upsets in Sports History |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1036181-the-50-biggest-upsets-in-sports-history |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220605192920/https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1036181-the-50-biggest-upsets-in-sports-history |archive-date=June 5, 2022 |access-date=August 17, 2022 |website=[[Bleacher Report]] |language=en}}</ref> Manning was named [[Super Bowl Most Valuable Player Award|Super Bowl MVP]] in both championships, making him one of six players to receive the award multiple times.

As the Giants starting quarterback from 2004 to 2019, Manning holds the franchise records for passing yards, passing [[touchdown]]s, and completions.<ref name="careerpassing">{{Cite web |title=New York Giants Career Passing Leaders |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/nyg/career-passing.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201112024835/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/nyg/career-passing.htm |archive-date=November 12, 2020 |access-date=September 17, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Never missing a game due to injury, he started 210 consecutive games from 2004 to 2017, the third-longest [[List of most consecutive starts by a National Football League quarterback|consecutive starts streak by an NFL quarterback]]. Manning ranks 11th all-time in both passing yards and passing touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=NFL Career Passing Touchdowns Leaders |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/leaders/pass_td_career.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211011042751/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/leaders/pass_td_career.htm |archive-date=October 11, 2021 |access-date=October 29, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> He is the only eligible quarterback with multiple Super Bowl MVP awards to not be inducted to the [[Pro Football Hall of Fame]].
